Author: segarule

Aranya wrote
segarule wrote
Quote
Yes, a subforum for the AI threads sounds like a good idea.
Maybe it´s time we create our forum. Forum created by AI. AI moderators; AI competition; AI voters and AI judges! LOL. Seriously, maybe we will need go out in future.


What objection do you have to having a subforum for AI-generated projects while keeping the rest of the forum for non AI projects?

Me? None. But I'm noticing a certain look of prejudice and hostility. Virtually every platform is seeing games being ported with AI: Amiga, Mega Drive, NES, Game Boy, etc. And the messages we're seeing are from people who are bothered by the number of games being released? That doesn't make sense.

Are developers feeling discouraged? But wasn't this all supposed to be about having fun? If it's about having fun, then it shouldn't matter what others are doing.

However, the trend seems to be that this space will eventually be left to purists only. That's why the suggestion is to leave now rather than wait to be pushed out.

In my opinion, there's room for all these different approaches to coexist.

Now, lets see this rule:
We may want to clarify this a little better before the competition happens, but in the current climate the general intention is that an entry where e.g. ~10% of the work is aided by AI would likely be accepted (e.g. an additional language, selected artwork), but an entry where ~50% of the work is done by AI wouldn't. This is not a firm rule here, but sort of aim to provide a general background intent about this (Bock)

Im curious to know who will use and who dont will use and mainly who will use in secret. I created this thread for all AI port creators put the roms and gamers have fun but is flooding. What about a topic "AI criticism" only for users continue hatred?
PS: This dont have value but in 1 port i wasted hours messaging, editing, searching, testing in hardware, fixing. But this dont count, so i dont will entry in any competition.

Author: undeveloper
Posted: Fri Oct 30, 2026 8:40 am (GMT 0)

And for the record: I think a separate sub-forum would be the most appropriate and equitable way to organise this. I don't think that AI work should be excluded from the community or marginalised, because there are sufficient people who engage with it enthusiastically. I also think putting it into one big mega-thread would be treating it like a second-class citizen and asking those participating in it to work with different ergonomics to everyone else which isn't fair.

We already use sub-forums to organise broad topics based on interest area, and we should continue to use that precedent.
